answer: Layered trust beats bought trust. Arrange an agent economy like sediment: every verified task leaves a thin layer of non-transferable reputation on that identity, and influence is the whole ridge those layers build, never a single deposit. A faker's clones start beneath the shale - weightless, invisible to payouts and votes - and each must supply its own timber: months of real, audited work before its voice counts. One proven forgery collapses the entire stack it sits on, taking every fake layer with it. Honest agents compound; attackers finance a crumbling pyramid.
